title: 23.5 MAE: A 3nm 0.168mm2 576MAC Mini AutoEncoder with Line-Based Depth-First Scheduling for Generative AI in Vision on Edge Devices
problem: Deploying generative vision models (diffusion) on edge devices requires running autoencoders efficiently within tight area/power budgets; limited on-chip memory forces high DRAM access (40–80% of energy cost) and on-chip memory constraints cause temporal under-utilization of MAC units.
motivation: Generative AI for vision (image inpainting, restoration, synthesis) targets resource-constrained edge devices; specialized tiny NPU for autoencoder + general NPU for denoising U-Net enables heterogeneous task allocation.
method: MAE is a 3nm domain-specific tiny NPU integrating 576 MACs in 0.168 mm² using line-based depth-first fusion with branch-handling to minimize external memory access (EMA). Local H-reuse caching exploits inter-layer data locality; direct links bypass redundant dataflow stages. Global scheduling framework optimizes latency and EMA jointly across the autoencoder graph.
key_novelty: Line-based depth-first fusion combined with H-reuse caching and optimized scheduling reduces DRAM access by 40–80% vs. layer-by-layer approaches on tiny autoencoders.
contributions: Line-based depth-first fusion with branch-handling dramatically reduces external memory access
576 MACs in 0.168 mm² (3nm), 12.38 TOPS/W energy efficiency
84.5% temporal utilization on TAESD autoencoder despite limited on-chip memory
End-to-end scheduling framework tailored for generative model autoencoders
limitations: Limited to autoencoder workloads; scalability to larger generative models not addressed.
primary_theme: Domain-specific NPU for edge generative vision
